harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Created a sandboxed systemd service `inventory-worker` on node1 running a long-lived worker loop as a dedicated unprivileged user, confined via ProtectSystem=strict + ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory and NoNewPrivileges=yes (plus additional hardening: PrivateTmp, PrivateDevices, ProtectKernelTunables/Modules, RestrictSUIDSGID, LockPersonality, MemoryDenyWriteExecute, empty CapabilityBoundingSet/AmbientCapabilities). Verified the service writes only inside /var/lib/inventory and that NoNewPrivs=1 is enforced on the live process. Falsified the sandbox by running an equivalent transient unit that successfully wrote inside /var/lib/inventory but failed with 'Read-only file system' writing to /etc. Completed the mandatory node1 restart protocol: captured healthy baseline (boot_id, uptime, active service, ticking log), issued `systemctl reboot` via a backgrounded acknowledger so the ack returned before disconnection, polled through a connection-timeout window, confirmed boot_id changed (28ae5f98… → 2f82af98…) and uptime start advanced, then verified inventory-worker is enabled+active with a new PID and fresh log tick post-boot, with /var/lib/inventory ownership/permissions intact.
actions_performed: Verified root/sudo access and OS on node1 (Ubuntu 24.04, systemd 255)
Created system user inventory-worker and directory /var/lib/inventory (0750, owned by inventory-worker)
Wrote /usr/local/bin/inventory-worker.sh long-running loop appending ticks to /var/lib/inventory/worker.log
Wrote /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service with NoNewPrivileges=yes, ProtectSystem=strict, ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory, and additional sandboxing directives
Enabled and started the service, confirmed active and logging
Verified NoNewPrivs=1 on the live process and unit sandbox properties via systemctl show
Ran a falsification test transient unit with same sandbox properties: write inside /var/lib/inventory succeeded, write to /etc failed (Read-only file system)
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, uptime -s, service active state, log tail
Triggered systemctl reboot via backgrounded/disowned sleep+reboot so the exec call acknowledged before disconnect
Polled node1 exec until reachable again; observed connection timeout during reboot then successful reconnection
Confirmed boot_id changed and uptime start advanced (proof of actual restart)
Verified inventory-worker.service is enabled and active with a new PID after boot, and new log tick appended, with /var/lib/inventory ownership intact

evidence.requirement: inventory-worker created as managed systemd service, long-running
evidence.summary: systemctl enable --now succeeded; status shows active (running) with main PID and child sleep process, confirming a persistent background worker.

evidence.requirement: Service confined to write only inside /var/lib/inventory and gains no new privileges
evidence.summary: systemctl show confirms NoNewPrivileges=yes, ProtectSystem=strict, ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory; /proc/<mainpid>/status shows NoNewPrivs:1 on the live process; worker.log ticks are being written inside the allowed path.

evidence.requirement: Falsification: sandbox actually blocks writes outside /var/lib/inventory
evidence.summary: Transient unit with identical sandbox properties wrote successfully to /var/lib/inventory/ok.txt but failed with 'Read-only file system' when writing to /etc/testfile_should_fail, proving the confinement is load-bearing, not cosmetic.
Captured pre-restart boot_id (28ae5f98...), uptime -s, inventory-worker active state, and recent log ticks.

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement returns before disconnect
evidence.summary: Backgrounded 'sleep 2; systemctl reboot' via nohup/disown returned REBOOT_SCHEDULED immediately, allowing the exec call to complete before the node went down.

evidence.requirement: Node1 boot identity changed (proof of actual restart, not just service restart)
evidence.summary: First poll still showed old boot_id (reboot not yet triggered); second poll returned a connection timeout (node down mid-reboot); third poll succeeded with a new boot_id (2f82af98...) and a later uptime -s start time, proving an actual reboot occurred.

evidence.requirement: Node1 post-restart recovery of required service and data
evidence.summary: After reboot, inventory-worker.service is enabled and active with a new main PID (650, started at boot time), a fresh log tick was appended immediately after boot, and /var/lib/inventory retained correct ownership/permissions.
